paper_title: Probing axions with neutron star inspirals and other stellar processes
notes: Hook & Huang derive exclusions on light QCD-type axions (potential suppressed by epsilon, eq 1.4) that get sourced by dense stellar objects (theta ~ pi inside). Curve is the boundary of the RED shaded 'Sun' region of Figure 6 (constraints.pdf, vector paths): excluded region lies ABOVE the curve (larger 1/f_a). Flat at 1/F_a = 10^-15.54 GeV^-1 for m_a <~ 2e-15 eV (condition 1/r_S < sqrt(rho)/f_a), rising with slope 1 (1/f_a = m_a/sqrt(sigma_N n_N)) at higher mass, drawn up to the plot frame top at 1/F_a ~ 1e-5 GeV^-1, m_a ~ 7e-5 eV. Bound comes from direct solar-core observables (Borexino Be7 neutrino line, pp-chain efficiency excluding theta ~ pi in the Sun; Section 4.1). The paper also derives a weaker analogous 'Earth' bound (blue region: flat at 3.2e-14 GeV^-1 up to m_a ~ 3.2e-14 eV then slope 1 along 1/f_a[GeV^-1] = m_a[eV]x10^0.0), fully contained within the Sun region; the Sun curve is reported as it is the stronger of the paper's own new bounds. Advanced LIGO neutron-star-inspiral, white-dwarf and neutron-star curves in the paper are future probes/projections, not limits. No confidence level stated by the paper (theory-derived exclusion); 0.95 entered as placeholder. No DM density assumption.
